messages.subject: [R-sig-Epi] AI-Assisted Data Analysis: Modern Workflows - AI workflows for epidemiology
messages.subject_clean: AI-Assisted Data Analysis: Modern Workflows - AI workflows for epidemiology
messages.body_plain:
Hello R-SIG-EPI members

A reminder - Epidemiological datasets require analytical workflows that remain inspectable from input to output. AI-Assisted Data Analysis: Modern Workflows is a seminar livestreaming October 6 with Kimberly Fessel (Dr Kim Data | Data Science Consultancy). Validate AI-generated Python code before using it to clean, explore, visualise, or analyse epidemiological data. Work with missing values, outliers, descriptive summaries, and charts while keeping statistical reasoning and data privacy central. Apply reproducible workflows to document analytical decisions in R-adjacent epidemiological research practice.

Details and registration: https://instats.org/seminar/ai-assisted-data-analysis-modern-workflo
Further information is available on the seminar page.


Best wishes

Michael Zyphur
Director
Instats | instats.org

messages.subject: [R-sig-Epi] Multilevel and Mixed Models for Epidemiology
messages.subject_clean: Multilevel and Mixed Models for Epidemiology
messages.body_plain:
Hello R-SIG-EPI members

A reminder - A rigorous approach to dependent observations can sharpen epidemiologic inference. Multilevel and Mixed Models with AI is a 2-day seminar livestreaming October 7 and 9 with Michael Zyphur (Instats | instats.org). Model clustered patient, clinic, and repeated-measures data by separating within-group from between-group variation. Estimate mixed-effects models in R and Mplus, then diagnose convergence and specification problems. Apply mediation, moderation, and simulation to epidemiologic questions while documenting AI-assisted coding and interpretation.

Details and registration: https://instats.org/seminar/multilevel-and-mixed-models-with-ai
Further information is available on the seminar page.


Best wishes

Michael Zyphur
Director
